items.text: The Syariah Criminal Offences (Federal Territories) Act 1997 (Act 559) applies only to persons professing the religion of Islam. Section 19(1): consuming any intoxicating drink in any shop or other public place is an offence, with a fine not exceeding RM 3,000 (about A$1,052) or imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or both. Section 19(2): making, selling, offering or exhibiting for sale, keeping or buying any intoxicating drink is an offence, with a fine not exceeding RM 5,000 (about A$1,753) or imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years, or both.

psychoactive-substances.notes: This Act applies only to persons professing the religion of Islam, and only in the Federal Territories named in section 1(2) (Kuala Lumpur and Labuan). It is not the Syariah enactment of any other Malaysian state. This is the official English reprint incorporating amendments up to 1 January 2006; later amendments were not on the file read. Ringgit converted at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026 (A$1 = MYR 2.8530). The Act is the destination's own source and leads.

items.text: Act 559 applies only to persons professing the religion of Islam. Section 2 defines zina as sexual intercourse between a man and a woman out of wedlock. Section 23: a man who performs sexual intercourse with a woman who is not his lawful wife, or a woman who performs sexual intercourse with a man who is not her lawful husband, is liable to a fine not exceeding RM 5,000 (about A$1,753) or imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or whipping not exceeding six strokes, or any combination. Pregnancy out of wedlock as a result of consensual intercourse is prima facie evidence against the woman (section 23(3)); birth of a fully developed child within six qamariah months of marriage is deemed pregnancy out of wedlock (section 23(4)). Section 24: an act preparatory to sexual intercourse out of wedlock carries a fine not exceeding RM 3,000 (about A$1,052) or imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or both.

Act 559 applies only to persons professing the religion of Islam. Section 2 defines liwat as sexual relations between male persons and musahaqah as sexual relations between female persons. Section 25 (liwat) and section 26 (musahaqah) each carry a fine not exceeding RM 5,000 (about A$1,753) or imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or whipping not exceeding six strokes, or any combination.

Act 559 applies only to persons professing the religion of Islam. Section 27 (khalwat): a man found together with one or more women who are not his wife or mahram, or a woman found together with one or more men who are not her husband or mahram, in any secluded place or in a house or room under circumstances which may give rise to suspicion that they were engaged in immoral acts, is liable to a fine not exceeding RM 3,000 (about A$1,052) or imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or both.

Act 559 applies only to persons professing the religion of Islam. Section 28: a male person who, in any public place, wears a woman's attire and poses as a woman for immoral purposes is liable to a fine not exceeding RM 1,000 (about A$351) or imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year, or both. Section 29: acting or behaving in an indecent manner in any public place, contrary to Islamic Law, carries a fine not exceeding RM 1,000 (about A$351) or imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or both.

Smartraveller: Malaysia enforces some aspects of sharia law. These laws apply to all Muslims, including visitors from Australia. The destination's own statute (Act 559) leads on the offences and penalties; this advice is the second-choice source.
